To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p65 concentration significantly increased and p50 binding activity significantly decreased in breast carcinoma.
p65, p 50 and CAIX are not related to tumor stage, however p50 binding activity is related to tumor grade.
RelA/p 65 concentration increased in breast carcinoma irrelevant to tumor stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hypoxia and NF- in breast carcinoma, which is an important factor to understand the pathogenesis of breast cancer and may be used to develop novel therapeutic targets.
the role of NF-B and its subunits p65 and p50 and CA IX as markers for breast cancer.
the relation between NFB family members, CAIX, tumor stage, and breast carcinoma subtypes in IDC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relation of the studied markers to tumor stage is unclear, and more studies are needed to clarify this issue.
the relation between hypoxia markers p65, p 50, and CA IX in IDC subtypes is not clear and needs more investigations.
the expression of p65 and p50 and CA IX in breast cancer are associated with poor prognosis and that these proteins may serve as biomarkers of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypoxia induced markers, p65 and p50, might be involved in the development of breast carcinoma.
, p50 might be a potential prognostic marker in IDC and CAIX concentration may be used as a prognostic marker for the number of the affected lymph nodes.
p65 and p50 expression is not related to the stage of breast cancer, however p50 binding activity and CAIX protein concentration are associated with tumor stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p65, p65, CAIX and IDC subtypes are independent factors in the progression of breast carcinoma.
the hypoxic markers p65, p 50, and CA IX might be used as a prognostic marker in IDC.
the expression of p65 and p50 and CA9 in breast cancer tissues are independent of the tumor grade, stage, and nodal status.
